minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard the school FY22 budget and reviewed money warrant articles; no votes beyond adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the superintendent and business manager present the school department's recommended FY22 budget, then asked about staffing, guidance cuts, math, morale and capital. It then walked through the money warrant articles ahead of next week's public hearing, and debated the school fire alarm replacement and a possible Town Meeting amendment. Only adjournment was voted.

public_comment.topic: A member suggested a separate focused discussion on personnel and compensation after Town Meeting.
A member asked residents to report broken or missing street lights to the DPW with the pole number.

votes.outcome: passed by roll call; members voted aye

budget_items.what_was_said: The recommended school budget is a modest percentage increase, compared with the prior two years' increases.
Budget covers contractual increases, flat health insurance, transportation, new positions and a salary reserve while four unions negotiate.
Chapter 70 is per the Governor's budget without the hold harmless; circuit breaker is expected to cover part of costs; grants expected level funded.
A member questioned how much the enrollment difference would change Chapter 70; the superintendent said impact is small for Lunenburg but larger elsewhere.
Costs for the full return are being encumbered against the local budget and may later be charged to grants.
Business manager said an involuntary transfer within contract has no financial impact.
A local curriculum adoption line is earmarked to fund new math programs alongside the math specialist.
A member noted capital work at the primary school is not being done this year.
Amendment article will cover the snow and ice deficit if not covered within appropriation.
After the fuel tank project, surplus is available toward capital.
Recommend maintaining a deposit from free cash into stabilization, which keeps the balance above the minimum.
Town manager prefers depositing rather than withdrawing for a DPW purchase, aiming to fund fire apparatus; balance and needed amount stated.

Recommendation maintained for savings to town and school from premium holiday.
Appropriation from lot sales for care of cemeteries, in addition to operating budget.
Articles rescind unborrowed authorization for school project, which MSBA funded.
Survey update to be paid from this year's facilities budget.
Agricultural preservation restriction covers acreage with a gift of land; a member wants full view of benefit.
State earmark must be used by June 30 2021; extension needs legislature; project cost estimated.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the school department's recommended FY22 budget, which the presenters described as a modest percentage increase over the prior two years.
The presenters said the budget covers contractual increases, flat health insurance, transportation, new positions and a salary reserve while four unions negotiate.
Members asked about Chapter 70, enrollment, circuit breaker and COVID costs; Chapter 70 follows the Governor's budget without hold harmless, and full-return costs are being encumbered locally.
The committee walked through the money warrant articles, including a snow and ice deficit amendment and a stabilization deposit from free cash.
Members debated the school fire alarm and a possible Town Meeting amendment; no resolution was reached, and the only vote was adjournment.

why_it_matters: The school budget is the largest piece of what the town raises, and the salary reserve means pay costs for four unions are not yet settled in the FY22 request.
The fire alarm earmark, snow and ice deficit and stabilization deposit are warrant articles residents will be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Public hearing next Thursday at 7, followed by Finance Committee votes on warrant recommendations.
The Finance Committee warrant letter, to be discussed publicly after that hearing.
